articles.heading: Fair Play and Use of Notes
articles.content: The players shall take no action that will bring the game of chess into disrepute. During play the players are forbidden to use any notes, sources of information or advice, or analyse on another chessboard. The scoresheet shall be used only for recording the moves, the times of the clocks, offers of a draw, matters relating to a claim and other relevant data.

articles.heading: Electronic Devices
articles.content: During play, a player is forbidden to have a mobile phone and/or other electronic means of communication in the playing venue, unless the rules of the competition allow it. If it is evident that a player has such a device on their person in the playing venue, the player shall lose the game. The opponent shall win. The rules of a competition may specify a different, less severe, penalty.

articles.heading: Distracting the Opponent
articles.content: It is forbidden to distract or annoy the opponent in any manner whatsoever. This includes unreasonable claims, unreasonable offers of a draw or the introduction of a source of noise into the playing area.

articles.heading: Analysis in Playing Area
articles.content: Losers are not required to stay and shake hands. No analysis is to be conducted in the playing area during the round. Players who have finished their games must leave the playing area unless they have been given permission to stay by the arbiter.

articles.heading: Leaving the Playing Venue
articles.content: The players may leave the playing venue during the game only with the permission of the arbiter. The player whose turn it is to move is not allowed to leave the playing area without permission of the arbiter.

articles.heading: Illegal Positions and Pieces
articles.content: It is forbidden to use a source of information to reconstruct the game. If a player needs to leave the venue, they must have the arbiter's permission. Players must not make any move on the board that would be illegal under the Laws of Chess.

articles.heading: Infringements and Penalties
articles.content: An infringement of the Laws may result in penalties including the loss of the game. The arbiter may impose various penalties for breaches of the rules, including awarding extra time to the opponent, or declaring a loss for the offending player.
